by: converted (convert1d) from fact_check__1.json and the research's 7 searches

checks.claim: Roughly 40–50 mph (about 65–80 km/h) at full power, depending on the saw.
checks.why: Manufacturer chain speeds at max power convert to about 37–49 mph (Stihl 18.6–21.7 m/s is about 42–49 mph; Husqvarna 55–62.7 ft/s is about 37–43 mph). 50 mph is the top of the range, not typical. Only the ISO test maximum on big saws reaches about 60 mph.

sources.title: Find your class of chainsaw protection

checks.claim: Idle is typically about 2,700–3,000 rpm and the clutch engages at about 3,900–4,300 rpm, depending on the saw.
checks.why: Manuals show these figures vary by model (Shindaiwa idle 2,700 and engagement 4,100; Husqvarna 120: 3,000/4,000; 445: 2,700/4,300; 545 Mark II engagement 3,900). They are not universal.

checks.claim: A chainsaw engine can reach roughly 13,000 rpm at full throttle.
checks.why: No manufacturer or government source in the notes states a maximum engine rpm. Only blogs, Quora and forums give 12,000–14,000 rpm, which are unreliable.

checks.claim: Standards require a chain brake to stop the chain in about 0.12 seconds on average, and no more than 0.15 seconds.
checks.why: CCOHS (CSA Z62.1) and the NZ gazette give an average of no more than 0.12 s and a maximum of 0.15 s; this is about a tenth of a second but is a test limit, and real-world stopping depends on brake condition.

sources.title: Unsafe Goods (Chainsaws Without a Chain Brake) Indefinite Prohibition Notice 2012 - 2012-go3557
